records.query: Need the patient's echocardiography and CT pulmonary angiography reports to confirm the acute cardiopulmonary event, including right heart strain and pulmonary embolism burden, as these are core imaging findings for verifying this leading hypothesis.

Need the patient's cardiac biomarkers (troponin, BNP) and electrocardiogram to evaluate myocardial injury and arrhythmic burden, as these are core tests to verify an acute cardiopulmonary event and differentiate acute coronary syndrome or tachyarrhythmia from pulmonary embolism alone.

Need the patient's echocardiography results and cardiac biomarkers (troponin, BNP) as core evidence to confirm or exclude acute cardiopulmonary event, along with CT pulmonary angiography to assess thromboembolic burden.

Need the patient's electrocardiogram and lower extremity venous duplex ultrasound results to further verify an acute cardiopulmonary event; ECG can reveal ischemic or arrhythmic changes and duplex can identify a thromboembolic source supporting pulmonary embolism.

Need the patient's arterial blood gas and serial lactate measurements to quantify the severity of respiratory failure and shock, along with a chest radiograph to assess for cardiomegaly or pulmonary edema, which will help confirm hemodynamic compromise from the acute cardiopulmonary event.

Need abdominal imaging (CT) and blood cultures to exclude an intra-abdominal septic source, the main competing diagnosis, along with procalcitonin and serial lactate clearance to differentiate septic from cardiogenic shock, thereby consolidating the acute cardiopulmonary event hypothesis.
records.text: Multiple blood cultures, pleural fluid culture, and urine cultures showed no organism growth

records.query: Need the patient's abdominal CT with contrast to exclude an intra-abdominal septic source, given the presenting abdominal pain and shock; this is essential to differentiate the leading acute cardiopulmonary event from abdominal sepsis, while the already requested echocardiography, CTPA, biomarkers, and ECG will confirm the cardiopulmonary mechanism.

Need the patient's lower extremity venous duplex ultrasound to identify a deep vein thrombus as the embolic source, a core ancillary imaging finding that would confirm the pulmonary embolism mechanism of the acute cardiopulmonary event and guide anticoagulation intensity.

Need the patient's D-dimer and arterial blood gas results to support pulmonary embolism severity and right heart strain; D-dimer is critical for the diagnostic algorithm, and ABG would assess oxygenation and hemodynamic compromise. These complement the already requested CTPA, echocardiography, biomarkers, and ECG.

Need the patient's serum lactate and coagulation profile (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) to assess shock severity and bleeding risk, which are essential for safely initiating anticoagulation in suspected pulmonary embolism with right heart strain and for evaluating any consumptive coagulopathy. These laboratory results are the key missing data complementing the pending CTPA, echocardiography, biomarkers, and ECG.

Need the finalized CT pulmonary angiography and echocardiography reports to confirm or exclude pulmonary embolism with right heart strain; these are the pivotal pending studies that will definitively validate the leading hypothesis.

Need the finalized CTPA and echocardiography reports to confirm or exclude pulmonary embolism with right heart strain, along with cardiac biomarkers and ECG findings; these are the pivotal pending results that will definitively validate the acute cardiopulmonary event hypothesis and guide emergency management.

bindings.label: A 54-year-old man presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain and shortness of breath
Patient has a medical history of hypertension and subglottic squamous cell carcinoma, treated with cisplatin and radiation therapy 8 months prior
Physical examination showed signs of respiratory distress; the patient rapidly deteriorated, requiring intubation and hemodynamic support with norepinephrine, phenylephrine, and vasopressin
Hospital course lasted 2 months and was complicated by pulmonary embolism, atrial fibrillation, and gastrointestinal bleeding
Echocardiography, CT pulmonary angiography, cardiac biomarkers, and ECG have been requested but results are not yet available
The acute cardiopulmonary event may be due to pulmonary embolism with right heart strain and/or myocardial injury
Blood and fluid cultures returned negative
Abdominal CT and venous duplex have been requested but results are not yet reported
Acute cardiopulmonary event due to pulmonary embolism with right heart strain
Acute cardiopulmonary event due to acute myocardial injury/infarction
Acute cardiopulmonary event due to hemodynamically significant arrhythmia (new atrial fibrillation)
Acute cardiopulmonary event due to combined pulmonary embolism and myocardial injury
Peripheral blood flow cytometry identified a clonal T-cell population comprising 18% of lymphocytes
